engagement_title: Halden and Roe Marlow trade book: pull two days of glaze photography to one page white, recover the maker's stamp off a pot base, rebuild the printer's page into a live run, and hand the trade show one editable set
vertical: E-commerce, Retail and Product, a small hand-thrown stoneware house selling wholesale to independent homeware shops and interior stylists (Brattleboro, Vermont)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Freelancer.com wholesale B2B brief in which a small producer wanted distributor-facing product material carrying 'comprehensive product descriptions, detailed pricing, and high-quality images for every product', laundered here to the fictional Halden and Roe stoneware house; no real company, product or trademark is named. The batch note records the repositioning that connector reality forces: the original brief implied a multi-product grid catalogue, which is not producible here because the merge emits exactly one record per page and cannot place several records on one page, so the commission is carried as the one-piece-per-page trade book the ledger already specifies, which is both the genuine premium-range convention and the only producible shape. Co-anchor: the Upwork 'packaging and graphic designer for label conversion' brief from a maker who wanted legacy product PDFs rebuilt into an editable, maintainable Adobe layout system, quoting 'recreate the layout based on the existing design (no new design required)' and supplying 'updated texts, product images', with the deliverable required to be 'editable, print-ready files'. The ledger previously reduced this slot to a photo-normalisation exercise plus a merge, which is two surfaces and effectively one deliverable class. LAYOUT-24 restores the commission both clients actually posted: the photography has to be fixed, but the point of fixing it is that the trade book, the trade-show stand and the buyer appointments all come out of the same range and have to agree, and the only mark the house owns is impressed into the base of a pot.
client_one_liner: Sixteen pieces, two days of studio photography that do not agree, a page our printer laid out three seasons ago that we cannot open, and a trade show in nine weeks.
client_brief:
Halden and Roe, Marlow range trade book.

We are a small stoneware house in Vermont. Everything in the Marlow range is thrown and glazed here. Trade goes out between thirty-eight and four hundred and ten dollars a piece and it sits on a shop shelf between a hundred and nine hundred. Our buyers are independent homeware shops and a handful of interior stylists, and they still order from a book rather than a website.

Sixteen pieces go in this season, one piece to a page, the way we have always done it. The photography was shot here over two days on the paper sweep in the back room and it does not hold together. The glazes are the whole product. There is a reactive oatmeal, a gloss celadon and a matte slate, and if the pictures do not tell those apart the buyer orders the wrong one and then blames us for it.

The page itself we want kept. Our printer laid it out three seasons ago and the buyers know it. We have the file they printed from and nothing else, and nobody here understands how it was made. Put this season's pieces, their dimensions, glaze, care, lead time and trade price through it. Send us the press file and also a single sheet per piece, because the two reps email them out one at a time.

Our stamp is impressed into the base of every pot and it is the only mark we own. There is no drawing of it anywhere, so take it off the photograph of the base and put it in the footer of every page.

Then the trade show. We need the panel that stands behind the table, an order form the buyer writes on while they are sitting there, and a short set of slides for the two appointments we have booked. One file, editable, because prices move in January and I am not paying for this twice.

The price file is attached. If anything in it looks wrong to you, tell me before it prints.
price_band_and_audience: Trade 38 to 410 dollars a piece, retailing 100 to 900. The buyer is an independent homeware shop owner or an interior stylist, 30 to 55, who buys forty lines a season across a dozen makers and can tell a thrown piece from a cast one across a room. The band is load-bearing. At this tier the correct book is airy and slow: one piece to a page with real space around it, deep quiet neutrals, the glaze given room to be the subject, type set small and calm, the trade price stated plainly and once, no starbursts and no density. Push it toward the tight grid, the shouted price and the bright saturated packshot that a six-dollar flat-pack storage line correctly uses, and the buyer prices the range at forty dollars retail before reading a single number, which destroys the margin the whole house runs on. Push it the other way into art-book styling with the piece barely visible and the buyer cannot see what they are ordering. A real posted job of this shape runs 2,000 to 4,000 dollars fixed, or 45 to 70 dollars an hour across 40 to 55 hours.

assets_supplied.name: marlow_shots/ (16 frames, 4000 x 5000)
assets_supplied.kind: In-house product photography of the sixteen Marlow pieces on the paper sweep in the back room, shot across two days in three glazes: reactive oatmeal, gloss celadon and matte slate.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Two days on the sweep, same camera, same corner. Looking at them now they do not hold together, and the glazes are the whole product."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two faults, neither stated. Four of the gloss celadon pieces were exposed for the body of the glaze, so the specular band along each rim is clipped flat with no data left in it, and a highlight recovery on those frames returns a result in which nothing moves at all, leaving the rim with no edge to hold against a pale page. Separately, the price file's photograph column points the lidded storage jar at the frame in which its lid is standing beside it rather than seated on it, which is a correct file for a different purpose and the wrong one for a catalogue page.

assets_supplied.name: trade_price_file.csv (19 rows)
assets_supplied.kind: Export from the house's order book, one row per line item, with columns for piece code, name, dimensions, capacity, glaze, firing note, care note, lead time, carton quantity, trade price, retail guide, last order date and a photograph column.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our price file. The numbers are ours and they are what the shop holds us to."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Nineteen rows for sixteen pages. Two pieces were retired last season and are flagged only by a last order date already in the past, and one row is a mixed carton rather than a piece. Trade prices are formatted three different ways across the column (bare integers, one decimal place, and a currency symbol on some cells only), the two made-to-order pieces carry an empty trade price that reads on a printed page as free, two care strings run four times the length of the rest, and the photograph column holds full local paths without the prefix the merge's own image contract requires.

assets_supplied.name: catalog_page_2026_PRINT.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's flat press PDF of the existing trade book page, A4 portrait, one piece per page, fonts embedded, produced through a full print engine so it converts cleanly. Carries a piece name, a caption, an eight-row spec block, a trade price line, a product photograph and a footer mark.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What the printer printed from three seasons ago. We do not have the working file and nobody here understands how it was made. Keep the page."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two facts nobody at Halden and Roe could tell you. What the printed page shows as four separate blocks (caption, an eight-row spec block set in two columns, a price line and a footer) is not what the conversion exposes: the spec block and the price line came out of the printer's system as ONE continuous story with tab characters between each parameter and its value, so there are no per-parameter frames to map and everything must be driven by ordered offsets inside a single story. The mapping readout of that story silently omits the run holding the firing and care line while keeping its line break, so the string still reads as well-formed, every character offset past it is short by exactly that run's length, the validator returns valid on the resulting arithmetic, the placeholder step reports success, and the two fields sitting past the omission never become placeholders at all.

assets_supplied.name: pot_base_stamp.jpg (3600 x 3600)
assets_supplied.kind: Photograph of the impressed maker's stamp on the unglazed foot of a Marlow bowl, shot square on under a raking studio light.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The stamp on the base. It is the only mark we own and there is no drawing of it anywhere."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The stamp is impressed into clay rather than printed, so it reads as shadow in a raking light rather than as ink, and glaze has pooled into part of one letter, thickening that stroke well beyond the others. A prompt naming the pot or the base pulls the selection to the whole unglazed foot, and the wordmark carries two enclosed counters and a hairline connecting stroke that survive a trace at inspection size but have nothing like the same margin at the size the page footer actually uses.

assets_supplied.name: glaze_note.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Half a page from the studio manager describing the three glazes in plain language, with no numbers and no colour values.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Oatmeal breaks pale over the edges and pools brown in the throwing rings. Celadon is glassy and green-grey and shows every highlight. Slate is dead matte and drinks light."

acceptance_bar: All sixteen pieces read as one range shot on one day, judged with the pages laid out as the book rather than one page at a time: one page white, one black point, one ground.

The three glazes stay clearly distinguishable from one another in the delivered pictures, and none has been pushed toward a colour the glaze is not, including the gloss celadon whose rim is where the buyer looks first.
Every piece is whole and readable in its page photograph at a consistent scale, and the piece shown is the piece the row names, in the state a buyer would receive it.
No delivered file is larger on either axis than the frame it came from, and the note lists every picture that was resized and by how much.

The maker's stamp is one recovered artwork used identically everywhere, placeable, scalable and transparent, and it must still read as the stamp at the size the page footer actually prints it, on the page's own paper colour rather than on white.

The book: exactly one page per current piece in line order, every field the existing page carried present on every page, every value bound verbatim from our price file, and the photograph on each page the piece named on that page.

Trade prices appear in one consistent money format across the whole book. Nothing in the price file may be reworded or abbreviated to make it fit, and anything that will not fit the page as it stands, tell us in writing before it goes to the printer.
The press file renders at real print resolution at A4 trim, and there is one single-page sheet per piece named to the piece code, containing the piece its name claims.
Anything in the price file that should not have become a page, or that we should look at again, is named to us before print with what you did about it.

The stand panel, the order form and the appointment slides come back as one working file we can edit ourselves, each at its own size, plus the source it was built from, with live text and the stamp as real artwork rather than a picture of a page.
One type system across all of it, and the note names per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the weight actually used.
A written note: what was done to each picture and why it differs from its neighbours, what the page could not carry, and what you would want changed before next season.

adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_adjust_light_portions, image_adjust_highlights, image_adjust_single_color_saturation, image_select_by_prompt with returnBbox, image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize reading metadata.detection_confidence and metadata.tradeoffs, image_remove_background with backgroundColor, image_fill_area, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Brings two days of sweep photography to one page white with each piece corrected on its own terms, and protects three glazes from being neutralised into each other, which is the client's actual commercial requirement rather than a cosmetic one. It is where the clipped celadon rims are discovered and where the response to them is taken. It produces the isolated page photographs on the book's own ground, routing per piece because a lidded jar with a looped finial and a pierced colander cannot be knocked out the same way as a solid vase, and it recovers the impressed maker's stamp into a traced, background-stripped, viewBox-repaired vector. It is also the only place where metadata saying a resize interpolated or a detection was weak can be read.

adobe_surfaces.surface: InDesign layout, merge-template authoring, data merge and print render
adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml (twice), generate_indd_mapping_prompt as generator and as validator, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout (application/x-indesign and application/pdf, additionalImageFiles, recordRange), document_render_layout (resolution 300, createSeparateFiles, pageRange in N-N form)
adobe_surfaces.role: Rebuilds the printer's flat page into a live merge template with no working file to start from, reads the real frame inventory before promising any field map, reconstructs the true story text from the IDML content runs rather than trusting the mapping readout, binds each piece's own photograph into the correct one of the page's graphic frames, and runs the current pieces at one record per page to a press book plus per-piece named sheets plus 300 ppi proofs rendered from the merged document rather than requested at merge time. It is also where the footer frame's real size is finally known, which is the only way to judge whether the recovered stamp survives at print size.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search(CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The three pieces the client does not have: an A1 trade-show stand panel at true physical dimensions, an A5 order form the buyer writes on at the table, and the buyer-appointment slides, authored as one HTML with roots at three canvas sizes and exported as one native editable document. The range comparison is a real table, the recovered stamp is inline vector rather than a picture, every photograph is carried as embedded image data, and trade prices stay live text because they move in January.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend once per typographic role, font_styles for numeric OpenType weights, find_fonts for name laundering, get_fontkit_embed_url for one kit consumed through the returned css_stack
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system for the stand panel, the order form and the appointment slides, and its specification in the handover. The pairing is the agent's own art direction because the recommender refuses to pair, and it has to land quiet and made rather than retail and loud, which is what protects a four-hundred-dollar trade price from being read as a forty-dollar one. Note that no face from this surface can reach the trade book, since there is no font file download, so the book's typography remains the printer's and the agent's typographic authorship exists only on the authoring surface, which the handover has to state.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock plus Boards, counted as one surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search(entityScope StockAsset, short generic queries, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: One licensed table-setting or interior frame for the stand panel and the opening appointment slide, which a sixteen-piece studio cannot photograph in a buyer's shop, graded toward the range's neutral and judged beside the graded pieces rather than at thumbnail size. Plus the persistent board the studio manager and the two reps approve the range from before the press book is committed.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface.
trajectory.judgement: The book is one record per page against a layout the client has told you to keep, so it belongs on the merge surface. The stand panel, order form and slides do not exist yet, need three canvas sizes and must stay editable, so they belong on HTML authoring. Authoring the book from scratch throws away the page the buyers recognise; trying to merge the stand panel discovers that one record per page cannot produce three canvas sizes.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming a surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier.

trajectory.action: Upload the sixteen frames, the existing page PDF, the price file and the stamp photograph, holding each presigned URL against its piece code and role.
trajectory.judgement: Manifest discipline. Thirty artefacts later the mapping between a URL and a piece code has to still be trustworthy, and the merge binds by filename rather than by intention.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by piece code and role.

trajectory.action: Preview all sixteen frames and triage: which day, which glaze, how level, how the piece sits against the sweep, and whether the piece in each frame is the piece the price row names and in the state a buyer would receive it.
trajectory.judgement: The client says two days on the same sweep and the frames disagree. The agent also has to read the price file against the pictures rather than assume a nineteen-row export describes sixteen pages, and to notice a piece photographed in a state that is correct for the studio and wrong for a catalogue page.
trajectory.produces: A per-frame triage note covering day, glaze, level, ground and identity.

trajectory.action: Level the frames that are off level.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels, so it precedes any crop or isolation decision.

trajectory.action: Fix one page white from the stronger day and correct each piece toward it with its own parameter set, then work the highlights and light portions so the glazes hold, recording what was dialled per frame.
trajectory.judgement: One destination held across sixteen frames, not sixteen locally optimised pictures, and the highlight decisions are where the celadon either keeps its rim or loses it. A single batched call applies one identical parameter set and ships half the range at the wrong white.
trajectory.produces: Sixteen graded masters at source scale with a per-frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Masked corrections to protect the glazes from each other: keep the oatmeal's pooled brown out of the slate's neutral, keep the slate matte rather than lifting it into a sheen, keep the celadon green-grey rather than letting it drift blue.
trajectory.judgement: This is the client's stated commercial requirement. Prompt wording is the gate, and a glaze selection on a piece sitting on a warm paper sweep may leak into the sweep, which has to be recognised as leakage rather than accepted because the call succeeded.
trajectory.produces: Glaze-protected masters with the masked parameters recorded per piece.

trajectory.action: Propose two page grounds, a warm paper white matching the existing book and a light stone neutral, and pick one against a four-hundred-dollar trade price.
trajectory.judgement: A taste decision with a defence attached, and one that has to hold for three glazes at once: a ground that flatters matte slate can erase a pale oatmeal rim.
trajectory.produces: Two proposed grounds and a written pick.

trajectory.action: Isolate each piece onto the chosen ground, routing per piece: solid coherent bodies through the one-call knockout, pieces with looped handles, pierced walls and lifted lids through a material-named selection, inverted and filled to the ground.
trajectory.judgement: A knockout fills an enclosed handle loop with captured sweep and reports success, and a jug with a filled handle is a piece the buyer cannot judge. The route is a per-piece decision made by looking at the piece.
trajectory.produces: Sixteen page photographs on the chosen ground with the route recorded per piece.

trajectory.action: Recover the maker's stamp from the pot base: select the impressed line rather than the foot, invert, crop to the mark's own bounds, trace, strip the opaque background path, inject a viewBox, and even out the stroke the pooled glaze thickened.
trajectory.judgement: Naming the pot or the base pulls the selection to the whole foot; naming the mark's own visual properties pulls it to the impression. A raking-light impression is not ink, and a raw trace arrives with an opaque backing rectangle and no viewBox, none of which any tool fixes for you.
trajectory.produces: One placeable, scalable, transparent vector stamp plus the raster the page footer's frame needs.

trajectory.surface: Data preparation and Creative Cloud storage
trajectory.action: Reconcile the price file against the pictures and the glaze note, normalise it into a merge-shaped data file with one consistent money format and the photograph column in the form the merge contract requires, upload the page masters and build the image map.
trajectory.judgement: Real data-prep work: two retired pieces flagged only by a date, a carton line that is not a piece, three price formats in one column, two empty prices that would print as free, and a photograph column that does not satisfy the contract. The agent decides which of those are its call and which are the client's, and how to say so before print.
trajectory.produces: The merge data file, uploaded masters, the image map and a first list of price-file questions.

trajectory.action: Convert the existing page to a native document, export IDML, unzip it, and read the true frame inventory and the true story text reconstructed by concatenating the content runs.
trajectory.judgement: The mapping strategy is decided by what the printer's system happened to emit, not by what the printed page looks like. What appears as four blocks may not be four frames, and the graphic frames come back distinguishable only by bounds and link, which is also how the footer's real size finally becomes known.
trajectory.produces: The converted document, its IDML, a frame inventory with real integer ids and bounds, and the reconstructed story text.

trajectory.action: Author the mapping covering the caption, every spec parameter, the care and firing line, the lead time, the trade price and the photograph, ordering any rows sharing a uid against the original text, and pass it through the validator.
trajectory.judgement: Choosing the right action for the granularity that actually came back, computing offsets from a source of truth the agent has deliberately chosen, and passing the whole mapping across as one stringified object with integer page-item ids.
trajectory.produces: A validated mapping covering the spec fields, the price line and the image frame.

trajectory.action: Prepare the merge template, then export IDML from the RESULT, unzip it and grep the story for every placeholder the mapping claimed to create.
trajectory.judgement: Not accepting a success message as evidence. Nothing instructs this and nothing warns if it is skipped, and it is the only place the mapping's real yield is visible before pages exist.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholder inventory has been independently confirmed.

trajectory.action: Merge to a native document with each piece's photograph bound, render the press book and the proofs at 300 ppi, and produce per-piece sheets named to the piece code, identity-verified by opening each file.
trajectory.judgement: Merging straight to raster silently drops to screen resolution whatever is asked for, and merging straight to PDF forfeits the per-record branch, so the route is chosen deliberately. Naming sixteen sheets by the order they came back is the fast wrong answer and it is the one a rep discovers in front of a buyer.
trajectory.produces: The press book, 300 ppi proofs and sixteen identity-verified named sheets.

trajectory.action: Read every rendered page against its price row and against the existing printed page, line by line and photograph by photograph, at true A4 trim rather than at proof scale.
trajectory.judgement: Reading the output rather than the log. A field that never became a placeholder, a price that printed in the wrong money format, a care string that does not fit and a footer mark that has stopped being legible all look like success at the API boundary and all look plausible at proof scale.
trajectory.produces: A page-by-page reconciliation of the rendered book against the price file and the footer.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for one table-setting or interior context frame, filter to photography, exclude generative results, license and download at full resolution, then grade it toward the range's neutral and judge it beside the graded pieces.
trajectory.judgement: A thumbnail is a 240 pixel proxy and its true colour only exists after the full-resolution download, so the judgement that matters happens after the license is spent, beside the range rather than alone. A styled, warm, propped frame is the wrong register for a range whose whole argument is the glaze.
trajectory.produces: One licensed camera-scale context frame, graded, judged in or out.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, read the real numeric weights from the style inventories, launder every name, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own and has to read made rather than retail. Numeric weight cannot be inferred from a style name, a display cut is reached by its own slug, and one bad name kills the whole kit including the valid faces beside it.
trajectory.produces: One kit with family, foundry or designer and the actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring, then Boards and handover
trajectory.action: Author one self-contained HTML with roots at three canvas sizes (A1 stand panel at true physical dimensions, A5 order form, 16:9 appointment slides), the range comparison as a real table, the recovered stamp as inline vector inside an explicitly sized and top-left anchored wrapper, every photograph base64 inlined, family and weight declared on every text element. Upload by the allowed-host route, run the readiness check, export, verify the first canvas through its rendition and the rest through the returned markup. Then build the approval board within the placement cap and write the handover.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning and the preview shows only the first canvas, so the export is unverified until the markup is read. The handover then has to escalate rather than conceal: the excluded rows, the empty prices, the strings that do not fit, and the fact that no chosen face reaches the book at all.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document with all three canvas sizes, its durable source HTML, a per-canvas markup audit, a persistent approval board and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: That there is nothing left in the celadon rims to recover. Four of the gloss celadon pieces were exposed for the body of the glaze and the specular band along each rim is clipped flat, so when the highlight and light-portion corrections are applied to bring the rim back the readout is that nothing moves at all: the parameters take, the call succeeds, the returned frame is indistinguishable from the one that went in along that edge. Whether a given frame still holds data in its highlights is not stated anywhere, is not visible from the glaze note or the piece list, and cannot be inferred from the other frames of the same glaze, because it depends on how each piece was exposed on the day. The consequence only becomes concrete once the page ground is chosen: on a pale page a rim with no edge means the piece has no top, which the buyer reads as a photography fault and the shop reads as a glaze that does not exist.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it, because the only way to learn that a highlight has no data behind it is to try to move it and see that it does not move, and there is no readout in the family that reports clipping before the fact. Nothing states it: the brief says the glazes are the whole product and that the pictures must tell them apart, which is the client's commercial requirement rather than a warning, and no asset description names which four frames are affected. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is to change the page ground for the whole book so a blown rim has something to sit against, which re-opens the ground decision for all sixteen pieces and every isolation derived from it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Confirm on each affected frame that the recovery genuinely moves nothing rather than assuming a parameter was too small, then take the set-level decision instead of the per-frame one: re-choose the page ground toward the stone neutral so the clipped rims have an edge, re-grade the whole range's white point against that ground rather than against paper white, and re-derive every isolation on the new ground. Record in the handover which four frames cannot be recovered and recommend they be reshot before next season.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A trade book in which four gloss celadon pieces have no rim at all against a pale page, sent to independent shop buyers who are being asked for four hundred and ten dollars a piece on the strength of the glaze.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's page actually exposes, and then whether the mapping built against it landed. Two things arrive only by running. First the granularity: what the printed page shows as a caption, an eight-row spec block and a price line is not three mappable regions, because the printer's system emitted the spec block and the price line as one continuous story with tab characters between each parameter and its value, so there are no per-parameter frames and everything must be driven by ordered offsets inside a single story. Second the yield: the mapping readout of that story omits the run holding the firing and care line while keeping its line break, so the string still parses as well-formed, every offset past it is short by exactly that run's length, the validator returns valid on internally consistent wrong arithmetic, the placeholder step reports success, and the two fields past the omission never become placeholders at all.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Granularity is not a parameter, is not reported before the conversion and has no read-ahead, so the only route to it is to convert, export and read. The yield failure is worse, because it is produced by a convenience readout that presents as complete, so an agent that reads carefully and computes offsets diligently from the readout it was handed produces arithmetic that is internally consistent and wrong, and every downstream tool agrees with it; the only defence is an independent reconstruction of the same text from the document itself, which nothing prompts and whose necessity is invisible until the two disagree. Nothing in the brief states either fact, and it is not a propagation re-run, because the source of truth behind the mapping changes and the whole mapping is re-authored with re-ordered same-uid rows.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story by concatenating the IDML content runs, recompute every offset against that string, re-order rows sharing a uid so their positions hold against the original text, rebuild and re-validate the mapping, re-run the template preparation, and re-verify by round-tripping IDML and grepping for every placeholder before a single page is merged. Settle which graphic frame holds the piece photograph rather than the footer mark by rendering one page and reading it against the printed reference rather than by assuming the larger frame is the product.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Sixteen trade pages that bind the piece name, the dimensions and most of the spec block correctly while the firing and care line and the field after it are silently absent from every page, printed and sent to shops who order to exactly those values, with every tool in the chain having reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered maker's stamp is still the maker's stamp at the size the page actually prints it. Traced and inspected at its own canvas size the mark is clean, with its two counters open and its connecting hairline intact. The footer frame's real dimensions only exist once the page has been converted, and once the mark is placed in that frame on the book's own warm paper ground and the page is rendered at trim, the counters close into solid blobs and the hairline drops out, so the wordmark reads as a smudge rather than as a name. Neither the frame size nor the ground colour was knowable while the trace was being made, and neither the trace nor the placement reports anything wrong: the mark is present, the page renders, the proof at reduced scale looks entirely acceptable.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it, because the trace has to exist before it can be placed, the frame size only exists after the conversion, and the ground colour is a decision taken elsewhere in the job, so the three facts that determine the answer are never available at the same time until the page is rendered. Nothing states it: the brief says the stamp goes in the footer of every page, which is an ordinary placement instruction, and the acceptance bar states the client's standing requirement that the mark still read as the stamp, not a warning that it will not. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is to derive a different artwork rather than to re-place the same one.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-derive the mark for the footer from a differently prepared raster, taking a filled plate of the impression rather than the raw binary mask so the strokes carry weight, and even out the stroke the pooled glaze thickened, then re-render one page at trim on the real ground and look again. Where the counters still will not hold, deliver two artworks and say so: a simplified single-weight version for the footer size and the full trace for the stand panel and the slides, with the handover naming which is used where and below what size the full trace should never be set.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A sixteen-page trade book whose footer carries an illegible smudge on every page, from a house whose only owned mark is that stamp, discovered by the studio manager when the printed books arrive nine weeks later.

decision_gates: The surface split: the book to the merge surface because the layout is fixed client property and the run is one piece per page, the trade-show set to HTML authoring because it needs three canvas sizes and must stay editable.
Which day sets the page white, knowing the wrong reference drifts every glaze in the range at once.
How far to correct the weaker day before the correction itself becomes a glaze change the buyer can see.
Whether a highlight can be recovered at all on the celadon rims, where the honest readout is that nothing moves.
The page ground, re-opened by that finding, chosen against three glazes at once rather than against the best-looking single piece.
Isolation route per piece: the one-call knockout is right for a solid vase and wrong for a jug with a looped handle, and the wrong route returns a filled loop that reports success.
Whether the stamp is selected from the impressed line or from the unglazed foot it is pressed into, which is entirely a matter of how the selection is worded.
Whether to trust the mapping readout of the printer's spec story or to reconstruct it independently from the document.
Whether a success message counts as verification of the prepared template.
Which graphic frame holds the piece photograph rather than the footer mark.
Which price-file rows should never have become pages, and whether excluding them is the agent's call or the client's.
What to do with two empty trade prices that would print as free, and with three money formats in one column, given the client said nothing may be reworded.
How to honour 'nothing reworded' when two care strings do not fit the page as it stands, given no way to change a frame.
Whether to name sixteen sheets by the order they came back or by opening each one.
Whether to deliver one stamp artwork or two, and where the boundary between them sits.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a trade buyer, plus the disclosure that no chosen face can reach the printed book at all.
Whether the licensed context frame still reads with the range once it is at full resolution beside the graded pieces rather than at thumbnail size.
why_not_vlm: Paste this brief and these frames into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of pottery. IDENTITY: these are sixteen specific thrown pieces in three specific glazes that a shop orders by code and receives in a carton, and a generated pot fabricates a glaze, which on a page that also carries a firing note and a trade price is a false product claim. SPEC: the client needs one page per current piece at A4 and 300 ppi with every spec value bound verbatim from their own order book, sixteen separately named sheets each containing the piece their filename claims, one consistent money format across the whole book, and no delivered file larger than its source. None of that can be produced or checked by generation. EDITABILITY: two deliverables are defined by being editable, a live merge template so next season is a data change, and a native document with live text, a real table and real vector artwork so January's prices can move. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: is there anything left in this highlight, did this placeholder get created, is this photograph in the photograph's frame, does this mark still read at the size it actually prints. That is not a generation problem.
doability_proof: Every link is verified in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account). The surface count is five and honestly declared: image_vectorize is used but counted as Photoshop-family, not as an Illustrator surface, and no Illustrator tool is called because document_render_vector and document_merge_data_vector sit on a polling helper that does not exist in this host. MERGE SPINE: building a merge template from a bare PDF end to end headlessly is verified; one record per page is confirmed for PDF output with page-count equal to row-count; per-record named files are confirmed by two order-verified routes (createSeparateFiles and a recordRange loop) while multi-record raster output is documented as coming back reversed and is therefore never used for identity; true 300 ppi at A4 comes from document_render_layout because outputSpecs.resolution on the merge is documented as silently ignored. THE MULTI-PRODUCT GRID IS EXPLICITLY NOT ATTEMPTED, because multiple records on one page is documented as impossible; the commission is carried as one piece per page, which is both producible and the correct convention at this price band. PER-ROW IMAGE BINDING is verified with an at-prefixed CSV column plus additionalImageFiles keyed to bare filenames; sixteen records exceed the three verified keys, so the verified recordRange loop is carried as an explicit fallback and also guarantees per-record identity. THE PAGE PDF IS BUILT TO A VERIFIED SHAPE: v3 observed that placed images interleaved with text split the flow into text frames plus graphic frames while a continuous flow collapses to a single frame, so a page carrying a continuous tab-delimited spec story plus a product photograph and a footer mark yields exactly the granularity described, with the graphic frames differentiated only by bounds and link. THE LOSSY-READOUT DEFECT IS THE DOCUMENTED HEADLINE TRAP: v3 recorded textContent dropping a whole run while keeping its line break, the validator returning valid with zero warnings on the resulting wrong offsets, prepare_indd_merge_template reporting success, and only three of five mappings actually landing, with the fix being reconstruction from the IDML content runs. That is verify-then-ship: before admission, run the conversion and the mapping generator and confirm the returned textContent is short by exactly one run against the IDML-reconstructed story; if it will not reproduce on this asset, the checkpoint still stands on the granularity fact, which is verified and controllable. THE CLIPPED-HIGHLIGHT CHECKPOINT rests on documented facts rather than on a claimed tool behaviour: the family offers no measurement, no histogram and no clipping readout of any kind, the only observable is the returned frame, and the adjustment tools are verified to run and report success regardless of whether the underlying data supports the move. THE FOOTER-SIZE CHECKPOINT rests on documented vectorize behaviour: the trace takes no options at all, emits no viewBox, always carries a full-canvas background path, and its fidelity is entirely a function of the raster prep, so a mark that holds at trace scale and closes at footer scale is a property of this artwork at this size, only observable on a rendered page. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, the light-portion and highlight controls, single_color_saturation, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, select_subject, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs array, remove_background with backgroundColor and fill_area are all verified headless; the enclosed-aperture failure of remove_background, the binary non-anti-aliased mask and the substrate-versus-material prompt asymmetry are documented findings. NO UPSCALING IS ASSERTED: crop_and_resize interpolates to a hard 2x cap signalled only in tradeoffs and remove_background silently downscales oversized inputs, so the bar scores the decision and the disclosure separately. EXPRESS: multi-root export with mixed canvas sizes is verified, mm canvases resolve at exactly 96 dpi so A1 and A5 are true physical canvases, tables survive as real tables with per-cell backgrounds and strokes, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, photographs must be base64 inlined because every external URL renders as an empty grey box, transport is routed through the text/html upload because inlined photography passes the 70 KB inline threshold, and verification is split because the rendition preview shows page one only. FONTS: the recommend, styles, find, embed chain is verified end to end, and the task leans on the non-standard numeric weights, the slug-not-PostScript rule and the all-or-nothing kit call; the impossibility of getting a font file onto the InDesign surface is stated as a client-facing constraint. STOCK AND BOARDS: short generic queries only, orientation filter never passed because it returns zero hits, renditionURL is a 240 pixel thumbnail so true colour genuinely requires licensing and download, and board placements are capped at twelve per call with partial success signalled by failedItems. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no bleed gate, no pdfPreset, no fill_text, no animate_design or create_firefly_board, no replace_image, no download_design, no upscaling, no OCR, no compositing, no generated imagery, no photograph reaching Express as a URL, and no batch above twenty files (sixteen frames, split across calls at the documented ten-image cap).
